record.what_it_does: AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes and summarizes meetings.
record.auth_notes: The official hosted MCP server (mcp.otter.ai/mcp) uses OAuth sign-in. Otter's pricing page lists it on the free Basic plan. Claude's connector directory lists it as "Made by Otter.ai" with sign-in required. Composio already ships an OAuth-based otter_ai_mcp toolkit, so client registration for third parties works in practice; Scalekit attributes this to CIMD/MCP client registration. The REST Public API (api.otter.ai/v1) uses a static Bearer API key that a user creates in workspace Developer settings (max 2 per user). The REST API has no OAuth. The REST auth details are from secondary sources only (Scalekit, anythingmcp). Otter's own API docs page rendered no content.
record.access_notes: This record covers two surfaces. The MCP server, which is the surface the hint points to, is self-serve: Otter's pricing page lists "Otter MCP server" under the free Basic plan. OpenAI's listing notes that some workspaces need admin approval to connect. The REST API and webhooks are a different case. The pricing page lists "Otter API & Webhooks" only under Enterprise, which shows "Custom pricing" and "Schedule a demo", so that surface effectively requires a sales conversation (contact_sales).
record.api_breadth_notes: The MCP server has three read-only tools, confirmed on Claude's connector page: get_user_info, search and fetch. The REST API at api.otter.ai/v1 is Enterprise-only and also small. Per Scalekit it covers channels and members, conversations (list, retrieve, POST to ingest a file), audio download links and workspace details, with a limit of 10 requests per second. The REST endpoint list is not verified against Otter's own docs.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp uses Streamable HTTP and OAuth and has three read-only tools: get_user_info, search and fetch. Claude's connector directory lists it as "Made by Otter.ai" and Anthropic-verified. It is also listed as an OpenAI ChatGPT plugin. Otter's pricing page includes it on the Basic plan.
record.blocker_notes: A toolkit can be built today on the official MCP server: it uses OAuth, works on free accounts, and Composio already ships otter_ai_mcp. That server has only three read-only tools (search, fetch, user info). Fuller REST access and webhook triggers need an Enterprise plan (custom pricing, schedule a demo) and per-user static Bearer keys.

evidence.quote: The Public API is a REST surface at api.otter.ai/v1, available to Enterprise workspaces only.
There is no public API key for the MCP server, and no OAuth for the API.
It authenticates with a Bearer API key created in the workspace Developer settings
Only the API is event-driven. Otter webhooks push conversation and action-item events in real time
